- When sentiment is high (≥0.7) and forecast is flat or rising slowly, model tends to under-forecast sharp upward moves; correct by adding 2–5% to early forecast if sentiment >0.7.
- When sentiment is low (≤0.3) and forecast is rising, model often over-optimistic; correct by subtracting 2–5% from forecast if sentiment ≤0.3.
- After a sharp spike in price (true outcome > forecast by >5%), model often fails to correct downward; apply downward bias of 1–3% for next 3–5 days if sentiment drops.
- If forecast is trending upward but true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days of decline), reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 5 days if sentiment is neutral or declining.
- If sentiment history shows repeated high-low oscillation (e.g., 3+ swings in 10 days), model tends to over-smooth; use 3-day moving average of true outcome for correction if sentiment is volatile.
- For 30-day horizon, if forecast is consistently below true outcome by >3% over 5+ days, model is underestimating bullish sentiment; add 1–3% to forecast if sentiment >0.65.
- If forecast is consistently above true outcome by >3% over 5+ days, model is overestimating bearish sentiment; subtract 1–3% if sentiment <0.35.
- When sentiment is high but price drops sharply (e.g., >5% in 3 days), model often fails to adjust; apply downward correction of 2–5% for next 3 days if sentiment >0.7 but price drops.
